text: The tape read of rwb-document, the buyer-panel read of rwb-partner and the case read and move answer of rwb-case are consumed on their owners' published contracts and fakes from Day 1, are class C dependencies in fact, and are not added to the metadata, whose Contract dependencies row stays None as the plan states it.
why: Only rwb-document holds the tape, only rwb-partner holds the panel and the agreement and only rwb-case writes recovery_case, while no source publishes an operation name for the three rows and the plan carries no C row for this slice. Inventing a name or rewriting a plan row are both forbidden.

text: The masked data tape is the deliverable of RWB-S6-E5025-APP and a document of rwb-document, with the masking applied by the PII service; this story reads the tape reference and its masking-check outcome on the P5 contract and never rebuilds, re-masks, copies or stores the tape, and it writes no lot status of the opening because no source names one.
why: R-DS-10 builds the tape and R-DS-11 rejects it, both before this step; the S6 field list carries no tape field, no source publishes the tape read, and LOV-LOT-STATUS has no value for a data-room opening, so both the tape and the status would otherwise be invented here.

text: The lot status a data-room opening would carry is not named by any source, so this story writes no lot status: the opening is held on the case route state DATA_ROOM_OPEN and on the decision record, and status stays a read-only lot property against LOV-LOT-STATUS.
why: LOV-LOT-STATUS gives BUILDING, OFFERED, AWARDED, TRANSFERRED and CLOSED and none of them names a data room, while the route machine of TSD S6 T4 carries the opening as DATA_ROOM_OPEN on the case; choosing a lot value would be a business value invented by the builder.
